'verified' is false until a native speaker confirms it. confidence: 'reference' = Wikipedia/academic/news; 'informal' = blog/forum, check before demo. Kannada script marked kn_check:true was transliterated by the compiler, not given in the source.
meta.fields: english = meaning; standard = standard Kannada; dialect = regional form; type = word | phrase | grammar | sound | loanword

places.name: Mysuru
places.about: Often described as the prestige spoken variety, closer to written Kannada than Bengaluru speech and linked with the Wadiyar court.

places.name: Mandya
places.about: Sits between Bengaluru and Mysuru but has its own rural-flavoured speech; studied academically (University of Mysore PhD, 1991).

places.name: Nanjangud
places.about: Nanjangudu Kannada is listed as a distinct variety in Kannada dialect classifications.

places.name: Gundlupet
places.about: A town in Chamarajanagar district near the Bandipur forest. No words collected yet.

places.name: Bengaluru
places.about: Youth-driven vernacular full of slang and Kanglish, popularised by radio stations and picked up quickly by newcomers.

places.name: Kolar
places.about: Part of Morasu Nadu, where Kannada, Telugu and Tamil cultures blend; large Telugu, Urdu and Tamil speaking minorities.

places.name: Chikkamagaluru
places.about: Coffee country of Malnad. No words collected yet.

places.name: Shivamogga
places.about: Gateway to Malnad. Havyaka Kannada is common around Thirthahalli, Sagara and Hosanagara (see Sirsi entries).

places.name: Sirsi
places.about: A centre of Havyaka Kannada (Havigannada), a dialect that preserves Old Kannada features lost elsewhere. Uttara Kannada Havigannada resembles Kundapura Kannada. It is also called Havyaka Bhaashe or Haiga Kannada, and about 12 lakh people speak it across the coast and Malenadu.

places.name: Thirthahalli (Malenadu)
places.about: Malenadu Kannada is spoken by about 7 lakh people in the hill taluks of Hosanagara, Thirthahalli, Narasimharajapura, Koppa and Sringeri. Male means hill and nāDu means land: this is the land of the Western Ghats, and its words for the forest, plantations and areca are its own.

places.name: Udupi
places.about: Coastal Kannada blends influences from Tulu, Konkani and Beary and is tied to Yakshagana.

places.name: Mangaluru
places.about: Spoken with clear diction, close to how Kannada is taught in schools; used in historical and mythological films and plays. Fun fact: the city has different names in Tulu (Kudla), Konkani (Kodial) and Beary (Maikala).

places.name: Kundapura
places.about: Kundagannada is spoken in Kundapura, Byndoor, Brahmavar and Hebri taluks, with Tulu influence. A Kundapura Kannada dictionary exists. Shortening words is its standout feature. About 8 lakh people speak it, in Kundapura, Brahmavara, Byndoor and Hebri taluks and in Bhatkal. Every year Kundāpra Kannada Day is celebrated worldwide on the no-moon day of Āshāḍha (around June–July). The name may come from the Alupa king Kundavarma's Kundeshwara temple, or from kunda, jasmine, which grows everywhere here.

places.name: Sullia (Arebhashe)
places.about: Arebhashe, also called Aregannada or Gowda Kannada, is spoken by about 5 lakh people across Kodagu, Dakshina Kannada around Sullia, and Kasaragod in Kerala. Are means half and bāse means language: it is said to keep Kannada in a 'half' form. The Karnataka Arebhashe Academy was set up in Madikeri on 15 December 2011, and 15 December is celebrated as Arebhashe Day.

places.name: Ankola (Halakki)
places.about: Halakki Kannada, also called Acchagannada, is spoken by the Halakki community along the Uttara Kannada coast, in Karwar, Ankola, Kumta and Honnavar, by about 1.5 lakh people. They are mainly farmers, and the name may come from hālu (milk) + akki (rice), for a people who kept cattle and grew paddy.

places.name: Belagavi
places.about: Border region with heavy Marathi influence: Marathi loanwords for rooms, relatives and eateries, and Marathi numbers in rural counting.

places.name: Dharwad
places.about: Birthplace of Kannada linguistic nationalism. Described by CIIL as 'like jackfruit' – rough outside, sweet inside. Also called Hubballi Kannada, it is spoken by about 80 lakh people across the plains (Bayalusime). The name is said to come from dvāra (door) + vāṭa (town): for centuries it was a resting place for travellers and the gateway between Malenadu and Bayalusime.

places.name: Bagalkote
places.about: Bagalkote Kannada belongs to the North Karnataka group and is spoken across the plains (Bayalusime) by about 16 lakh people, in taluks like Badami, Jamakhandi, Mudhol and Ilkal. The name is said to come from bāgaDi, a bangle: a king of Bijapur gave the town to his daughter as a wedding gift.

places.name: Kalaburagi
places.about: Kalyana Karnataka speech incorporates Telugu, Urdu and Marathi elements, reflecting multicultural borderlands. Kalaburagi Kannada (also Gulbarga or Kalburgi Kannada) is spoken by about 18 lakh people across Kalaburagi and Bidar districts on the Deccan plateau. The name comes from kallu (stone) + burgi: a land of black stone.

places.name: Bidar
places.about: Dakhni Urdu has influenced local Kannada here more than anywhere else.
